summary.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 50.7% YoY to INR125.93 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 13.21% from 14.80% on input costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 50.70% YoY to INR1,259.34 million, with EBITDA (ex other income) up 34.51% to INR166.35 million. EBITDA margin contracted about 159 bps YoY to 13.21% as raw material, energy and logistics costs rose after geopolitical disruption. Consolidated order book was INR2,267.93 million at 30 September 2026, up from INR174.1 crore at 31 March 2026. Management said the major capex is nearing completion with phased commissioning, and guided to 20-25% annual growth and margin recovery to last-year levels within about two quarters.

segments.name: Heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Order book rose from INR142 crore (March 2026) to INR177 crore (September 2026); it is the largest order book component given long lead times and large order sizes.

segments.name: Wear plates and wear parts
segments.commentary: Order book rose from INR22 crore to about INR24 crore (INR249.62 million at 30 September 2026); lead time is 6-8 weeks.

segments.name: Welding consumables
segments.commentary: Order book rose from INR9.9 crore to INR24.9 crore (INR249.79 million); lead time is about 4 weeks or less. Flux-cored wire capacity is being increased.

segments.name: Roller press rolls
segments.commentary: Management expects roller press roll revenue of a little under INR100 crore this year; treated as an established product outside the new-initiatives bucket.

segments.name: New initiatives (shredders, VRMs, steel mill rollers, rotors/rotary air feeders)
segments.commentary: Contribute about 1-2% of revenue currently; management targets 10-15% of incremental revenue within 2-3 years. Loco shell manufacturing qualification received from Indian Railways.

segments.name: Joint venture (thermal spray powders)
segments.commentary: Reported a loss in Q2 FY27 versus about INR4 crore profit last quarter; management attributes this to the calendar-year seasonality of the JV, not to core operations.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to grow revenue 20-25% YoY, with an intention to exceed this, and said it is confident of 20%+ growth for 3-5 years.
Gross margin expected to recover to last-year levels (around 33-34% per analyst's reading) by Q4 FY27 if raw material prices remain stable.
Price pass-through lag estimated at 1 to 1.5 quarters; short-lead (under 6 months) orders are fixed-price, while longer orders carry price variation clauses.
Current INR226 crore order book expected to be executed within this year, with further order inflows expected.
JV expected to finish the calendar year on a higher note, with profit better than the first six months of that company.
Export expansion: Abu Dhabi facility coming live; Turkey operations stabilising; a large US order expected after tariff situation improved.
capex_capacity: Major capital expenditure is nearing completion; new manufacturing capacities are being operationalised in a phased manner.
Management said it has capacity to execute around INR140 crore in a single quarter, as achieved in Q4 FY26.
New capacity is expected to support larger and more complex specialised orders and improve utilisation, operating leverage and bottom-line contribution over coming years.
Abu Dhabi facility expected to go live; Turkey operations are being stabilised; Philippines subsidiary performing consistently better than last year.
Workshop space expansion is prompting customers to place more orders on the existing team.
demand_pricing: Core industries output grew 7.9% in September 2026 (highest in 30 months under new series); cement +9.8%, steel +4.9%, electricity +11.4%.
Business mix: about 30% of revenue from new project builds and about 70% from servicing, spares and maintenance of the installed base.
Input cost inflation from tungsten, specialty ferroalloys, metals and energy; tungsten has eased from peak but not to pre-Middle East war levels.
Price increases are being accepted by customers; quotations are being re-priced to current raw material costs and validity periods are being shortened.
Raw material sourcing: about 85-90% domestic and 10-15% imported; roller press forgings and castings are about 80-90% imported.
Exports to about 53 countries; new traction in Ghana (cement producer) and Nigeria; US order on hold due to tariffs expected to come through.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins bottoming and will raw material costs normalise over the next few quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price increases are being accepted and passed on, and tungsten has partly declined though not to pre-war levels; combined, this should consolidate margins.

qa_highlights.question: Segment revenue split for Q2 and H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give segment revenue breakup for competitive reasons, saying growth is occurring in all three segments; order book data was provided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the JV profit outlook given the Q2 loss?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV follows a calendar-year cycle with lulls in August, December and April; management expects a stronger finish by calendar year-end and says the swings are not operational.

qa_highlights.question: Will price pass-through apply to existing orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders under 6 months lead time are fixed-price, so cost increases must be absorbed; longer orders have price variation clauses. Current order book partly reflects higher input prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 a one-off high-execution quarter or a steady state? Any guidance revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 and Q4 have historically been strong, but the aim is a healthy order book across the year; guidance remains 20-25% growth with intent to exceed.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue will the new products contribute and how soon?
qa_highlights.answer: New entities contribute 1-2% of revenue now; management expects 10-15% of incremental revenue in 2-3 years, which would be about 15-20% of current revenue.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on raw material (tungsten, ferroalloys) and energy prices staying stable; management said further volatility cannot be predicted.
Fixed-price orders under 6 months expose the company to absorbing raw material increases until pass-through catches up (1-1.5 quarter lag).
JV (thermal spray powders) volatility: Q2 FY27 loss versus prior-quarter profit; management expects improvement by calendar year-end.
Execution in heavy engineering (3-9 month conversion) is longer; order book composition shifts revenue timing.
New initiatives (railways, defence, adjacent products) are long-gestation and currently contribute only 1-2% of revenue.
Monitor Q3 FY27 gross margin trajectory versus Q4 target of returning to prior-year levels, and commissioning progress of new capacity.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order book, with explicit cautions on input costs and margin pressure. Management was forthcoming on order-book movement and pricing mechanics but declined to disclose segment revenue split and the subsidiary performance figures, citing competitive reasons.
key_quotes: So, we expect to keep growing by 20 % to 25% as we have indicated before, and of course our intention and our effort is to do more than what we are committing.
I think it's fair to say within the next 2 quarters or so we should be able to get back to the same sort of margin levels.
But which has got nothing to do with our operations per se.
So, we don't see any slowdown per se, because as I mentioned, a major portion of our business comes from existing installed base and not from new capacity expansion.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided EBITDA margin back to prior-year levels by Q4 FY27 (Q2 FY27 consolidated margin 13.21% vs 14.80% a year ago), with price increases being accepted and a 1-1.5 quarter pass-through lag, provided tungsten and ferroalloy prices stay stable.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Major capex is described as nearing completion with phased commissioning, and the Abu Dhabi facility is expected to go live, though no capacity size or quarter is quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 20-25% revenue growth (H1 FY27 consolidated revenue +43.7% YoY) backed by a INR226 crore order book, up from INR174 crore at March 2026, and capacity to execute about INR140 crore per quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says major capex is nearing completion, and no new capex plan or utilisation figure was disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says it intends to exceed the 20-25% growth guide and expects a US order to come through once tariffs ease, but the margin guide is only a recovery to prior-year levels.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fixed-price orders under 6 months absorb input-cost increases until pass-through catches up (1-1.5 quarter lag), and management says further raw material volatility cannot be predicted.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New initiatives (shredders, VRMs, steel mill rollers, rotors) contribute 1-2% of revenue, with a target of 10-15% of incremental revenue in 2-3 years; the Indian Railways loco shell qualification is received, but no product launch date was given.

rows.label: INR226 crore order book to execute this year
rows.why: Order book rose to INR2,267.93 million at 30 September 2026 from INR174.1 crore at March 2026, and management expects to finish it this year while receiving orders daily.

rows.label: Abu Dhabi facility and US order
rows.why: Abu Dhabi facility is expected to go live, and a large US order on hold due to tariffs is expected to come through once the tariff situation improves; the timing is not given.

rows.label: JV (thermal spray powders) recovery
rows.why: The JV posted a Q2 FY27 loss versus about INR4 crore profit last quarter; management expects a stronger finish by calendar year-end and says the swings are seasonal rather than operational.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the INR226 crore order book and the 20-25% growth guide, and cautious on input costs and the margin hit; analysts pressed on margin bottoming and pass-through, and management declined to disclose the segment revenue split and subsidiary figures.
